content: Phytonadione, also known as vitamin K, is prescribed to prevent bleeding in individuals who have blood clotting disorders or insufficient levels of vitamin K in their body. It belongs to a class of medications called vitamins and works by supplying the necessary vitamin K required for normal blood clotting. Phytonadione is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It should be used exactly as directed by your doctor. In some cases, your doctor may also prescribe another medication, such as bile salts, to be taken alongside phytonadione. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not stop taking phytonadione without consulting your doctor. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, and do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than instructed. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking phytonadione, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to phytonadione, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in the tablets. Ask your pharmacist for a list of the ingredients. Do not take anticoagulants (blood thinners) such as warfarin (Coumadin) while using phytonadione unless specifically instructed by your doctor. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention antibiotics and salicylate pain relievers, such as aspirin or aspirin-containing products, choline magnesium trisalicylate, choline salicylate (Arthropan), diflunisal (Dolobid), magnesium salicylate (Doan's, others), and salsalate (Argesic, Disalcid, Salgesic). Your doctor may need to adjust the doses of your medications or monitor you closely for side effects. If you are taking orlistat (Xenical), take it two hours before or two hours after phytonadione. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking phytonadione, contact your doctor immediately. Discuss with your doctor the appropriate amount of vitamin K-rich foods to include in your diet while taking phytonadione. Do not increase or decrease your usual intake of foods such as green leafy vegetables, liver, broccoli, and cauliflower without consulting your doctor. If you miss a dose of phytonadione, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Inform your doctor if you miss any doses. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Phytonadione may cause side effects. If you experience unusual bruising or bleeding, contact your doctor immediately. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Protect phytonadione from light. Keep it at room temperature and away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to phytonadione. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist.
